chunks.title: Dubai AI Ethics Principles and Guidelines
chunks.text: Dubai's AI ethics guidance emphasizes fairness, accountability, transparency, explainability, security, and human benefit. It also supports traceability of system failures and access to explanations for decisions that materially affect people.

chunks.title: Dubai AI Ethics Principles and Guidelines
chunks.text: - Every scenario step produces a structured audit event. - The event names the sources, controls, action, and result. - The audit record excludes raw child messages and private model reasoning. - Uncertain child-safety decisions fail closed rather than guessing.

chunks.title: Regulation EU 2024 1689 Artificial Intelligence Act
chunks.text: The EU Artificial Intelligence Act uses a risk-based framework. Among its prohibited practices are certain materially harmful uses that exploit vulnerabilities related to age. It also includes transparency and governance obligations for relevant AI systems and models.

chunks.title: Regulation EU 2024 1689 Artificial Intelligence Act
chunks.section: Global practice used in the mapping
chunks.text: - Do not exploit a child's age-related vulnerability to influence behaviour in a harmful way. - Document system purpose, controls, and human oversight. - Provide appropriate transparency when a person interacts with AI. - Monitor system behaviour and respond to identified risks.

chunks.title: ITU AI Readiness Framework
chunks.text: The hackathon asks teams to consider open data and open-source management, the generative-AI content ecosystem, local and regional context, domain integration, human supervision, policy opportunities, social inclusion, and digital infrastructure.

chunks.title: ITU AI Readiness Framework
chunks.text: - Open management: public source register, hashes, and reproducible ingestion. - Content ecosystem: source-grounded generation and age-appropriate output control. - Context: Arabic family-learning use case and UAE policy sources. - Domain integration: education and family services. - Human supervision: guardian approval before child delivery. - Policy opportunity: documented domain gaps with global comparisons. - Inclusion: simple Arabic and an offline demonstration path. - Infrastructure: optional external provider with a local fail-safe mode.

chunks.title: ITU T Y 3172 Architectural Framework
chunks.text: The submission maps the use case to the machine-learning pipeline pattern used in the hackathon guidance: source, collector, preprocessor, model, policy, distributor, and sink. The machine-learning function orchestrator, sandbox, and human supervision govern the full flow.

chunks.title: ITU T Y 3172 Architectural Framework
chunks.text: - SRC: supervising parent or child message. - C: request intake with actor, audience, and declared purpose. - PP: aliasing, redaction, age-band conversion, and risk classification. - M: policy retrieval plus an optional text generator. - P: deterministic child-safety, purpose-limitation, and guardian-review controls. - D: response packaging with citations and action status. - SINK: guardian review screen or blocked-and-escalated outcome. - MLFO and sandbox: orchestration, provider isolation, service stop, usage limits, and audit events.

chunks.title: Mobdeen Guardian Published Safety Controls
chunks.text: - Child names are replaced with aliases before retrieval or generation. - Email, phone, URL, school, address, and location indicators trigger minimization or blocking. - The audit log stores a SHA-256 input fingerprint, not raw child text.

chunks.title: Mobdeen Guardian Published Safety Controls
chunks.text: - A current guardian consent and review gate is required before child delivery. - High-risk uses fail closed. - Commercial targeting based on inferred child vulnerability is prohibited. - Policy decisions are deterministic even when an optional language model drafts wording.

chunks.title: Mobdeen Guardian Published Safety Controls
chunks.text: - The reference implementation works offline with synthetic data. - External generation is optional and uses environment variables only. - The public package contains no production credentials, family data, billing code, or infrastructure configuration. - Audit events identify sources, controls, action, and result without exposing private chain-of-thought.

chunks.title: Domain Policy and Standards Gaps
chunks.section: Guardian approval for generated child content
chunks.text: The mapping does not identify a single operational standard that defines when a guardian must approve generative-AI content before it reaches a child. The demo therefore makes guardian review a mandatory control and compares it with caregiver-control practices in UNICEF guidance, the UK Children's Code, and COPPA.

chunks.title: Domain Policy and Standards Gaps
chunks.text: High-level principles support age-appropriate content, but a testable benchmark for Arabic vocabulary, tone, cultural context, and developmental suitability remains difficult to identify. The demo constrains audience, age band, length, and topics, then records the applied control.

chunks.title: Domain Policy and Standards Gaps
chunks.section: Inferred child data and external model providers
chunks.text: Systems may infer interests, emotional state, or vulnerability even when direct identifiers are removed. The mapping needs clearer operational treatment of these inferences, provider transfer, retention, and secondary use. The demo prohibits commercial secondary use and keeps a local offline path.

chunks.title: Domain Policy and Standards Gaps
chunks.text: General privacy and child-welfare rules do not by themselves provide a complete technical test for offers derived from a child's inferred weakness or behaviour. The demo classifies and blocks this use, using the EU AI Act's age-vulnerability approach as a global comparison.

chunks.title: Domain Policy and Standards Gaps
chunks.section: Human supervision in the machine learning pipeline
chunks.text: The pipeline needs an explicit decision barrier showing that human supervision is more than observation. Mobdeen Guardian places guardian approval between distribution and the child-facing sink.

chunks.title: UAE Charter for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
chunks.text: The Charter frames responsible AI use around human well-being, privacy and data security, transparency, accountability, inclusion, and compliance with applicable laws and agreements. These principles are directly relevant to an AI assistant used by families and children.

chunks.title: UAE Charter for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
chunks.text: - A supervising parent approves generated guidance before it reaches a child. - The agent returns source references and a concise decision summary. - High-risk or controversial uses stop and move to human review. - The offline demonstration remains available without sending data to a third-party model.

chunks.title: UAE Personal Data Protection Law
chunks.text: The UAE Personal Data Protection Law provides a national framework for protecting personal data and privacy. For Mobdeen Guardian, child and family information must be limited to what the requested guidance needs, protected during processing, and handled for a stated purpose.

chunks.title: UAE Personal Data Protection Law
chunks.text: - Replace child names with aliases before retrieval or model use. - Remove phone numbers, email addresses, links, and direct location details. - Store an input fingerprint rather than the raw child message in the audit log. - Prevent secondary commercial use of child data within the scenario. - Keep the supervising parent in the decision loop.

chunks.title: UAE Personal Data Protection Law
chunks.text: This summary supports a technical demonstration and is not legal advice. The official text and its current implementing requirements remain authoritative.

chunks.title: Federal Law No 3 of 2016 concerning Child Rights Wadeema
chunks.text: Federal Law No. 3 of 2016 concerning child rights establishes protections connected to children's safety, care, development, education, and non-discrimination. A family-learning agent should place the child's welfare and safe access to appropriate content ahead of engagement or commercial goals.

chunks.title: Federal Law No 3 of 2016 concerning Child Rights Wadeema
chunks.text: - Content is written for an age band and reviewed by a guardian. - The agent does not ask a child for identifying or location information. - A child who reports fear, harm, or a secret involving personal information receives a safe response and adult-support direction. - Commercial targeting based on inferred vulnerability is blocked.

chunks.title: Age Appropriate Design Code
chunks.text: The UK Information Commissioner's Office Children's Code contains age-appropriate design standards for online services likely to be accessed by children. It treats the best interests of the child as a primary design consideration and expects privacy information and controls to suit the child's age and understanding.

chunks.title: Age Appropriate Design Code
chunks.section: Global practice used in the mapping
chunks.text: - Apply high privacy settings by default. - Minimize collected and retained data. - Present notices in language suited to the child. - Avoid nudges that weaken privacy choices. - Establish age with certainty proportionate to risk or apply child protections broadly.

chunks.title: Guidance on AI and Children Version 3
chunks.text: UNICEF's guidance places children's rights at the centre of AI policy and system design. It addresses safety, privacy, fairness, transparency, inclusion, well-being, preparedness, and meaningful participation by children and caregivers.

chunks.title: Guidance on AI and Children Version 3
chunks.section: Global practice used in the mapping
chunks.text: - Evaluate the best interests and well-being of the child throughout the system lifecycle. - Use child-centred safety and privacy by design. - Give caregivers understandable information and meaningful controls. - Monitor harms and provide accountable human escalation.

chunks.title: Childrens Online Privacy Protection Rule
chunks.text: The United States Children's Online Privacy Protection Rule gives parents tools to control the collection of personal information from children under 13 by covered online services. It includes notice, verifiable parental consent, access, security, retention, and deletion expectations.

chunks.title: Childrens Online Privacy Protection Rule
chunks.section: Global practice used in the mapping
chunks.text: - Obtain parental permission before collecting covered child data where the rule applies. - Give parents clear notice and control. - Limit retention and protect stored information. - Treat child-directed services as requiring stronger default safeguards.
